messages:
incident-bot: INCIDENT: Latency SLO breach detected on inference-router-prod. p99=6.8s (SLO=3s), p95=1.9s, streaming stall rate rising. Paging oncall: @maya s. (oncall)

maya s. (oncall): I'm on it. seeing alert spike around 04:12 UTC. tagging eng-runtime and eng-platform.

jason (eng-runtime): grabbing traces. initial look: tail latencies concentrated on streaming/tail-endpoints (/v1/stream) and long token generation requests.

priya (eng-ml): are we seeing increased KV cache misses or model-side stalls? any change in recent model rollout?

jason (eng-runtime): no model rollout in last 12h per deploy-bot, but routing shows ~30% of requests getting routed to fallback-quantized variant.

deploy-bot: deploy: no user-initiated deploys in the past 24h. autoscaler adjusted pool size at 03:58 UTC.

sam (eng-platform): metrics: auth-service 5xx and 429 spikes coincident with the latency bump. configfetch p99 jumped from 80ms -> 1.2s around the same time. looks like control-plane deps slowing request path.

maya s. (oncall): copying relevant graphs: 
- router_p99: 6.8s
- streaming_stall_rate: 18% -> 37%
- auth_429_rate: 0.2% -> 4.5%

(not posting links in-thread, pulling dashboard snapshots)

lee (support): we have 3 customer reports from EU region about interrupted streaming sessions / stalled transcripts. severity = medium-high for affected users.

anita (product): which customers? are any paying enterprise affected? need to coordinate comms if high-risk.

rachel (cust-succ): flagged: AcmeHealth (enterprise, EU) and BetaAI (mid-market). AcmeHealth observed repeated stalls. I've DM'd Acme for timeline.

jason (eng-runtime): digging into traces -> majority of stalled requests show repeated auth retries with 429 or long auth latencies from token-store. sample trace excerpt:
```
CALL /v1/stream -> auth-service (200ms -> 1.3s retries) -> configfetch (1.1s) -> model-inference (fast) -> client stall
```
headers include x-rate-limit-remaining=0 in some cases.

priya (eng-ml): that suggests control-plane backpressure upstream of the runtime. KV cache misses + configfetch delay could be increasing request latency even if model is fine.

sam (eng-platform): confirmed DB connection saturation on configstore-proxy cluster (pool usage ~98%). error logs show `connection-timeout` and spikes in `SELECT` latencies. Looks like a fanout of config fetches hitting the DB.

maya s. (oncall): immediate mitigations we can do now (short list):
1) apply routing fallback to prefer cached model variants for streaming requests (reduce configfetch dependence)
2) rate-limit non-interactive endpoints at the router to reduce noise
3) temporarily increase configstore-proxy pool size (quick patch)
4) notify customers being affected and start postmortem tracking

sam (eng-platform): I can scale configstore-proxy pool now. doing:
```
kubectl -n infra scale deployment/configstore-proxy --replicas=6
```
Executing — will update when ready.

deploy-bot: scale triggered by sam at 04:24 UTC. replicas from 3 -> 6.

jason (eng-runtime): toggling router routing rule to prefer local cache for /v1/stream (will risk slightly stale flags but reduces fetches). patching traffic rules now:
```
PATCH /routing/overrides {"path": "/v1/stream", "cache_preference": "local-first"}
```

maya s. (oncall): doing coordinated rate-limit: apply 20% throttle to batch/async endpoints in eu region at edge for next 15m to reduce load.

priya (eng-ml): monitoring KV cache hit-rate... cache hit improves from 62% -> 89% after routing change. model latencies stable. streaming_stall_rate down from 37% -> 15% in last 4m.

sam (eng-platform): configstore-proxy pods are coming up; pool usage dropped to 65%. auth 429s reduced.

lee (support): customer update to AcmeHealth: "We've identified transient control-plane latency affecting streaming; mitigation in progress. We'll follow up with root cause and ETA for full resolution."

anita (product): good. keep comms short and frequent. prioritize AcmeHealth; loop in account exec.

jason (eng-runtime): still seeing a small tail at p99 ~2.8s, p95 ~1.2s. likely residual retries and circuit-closed warm-up. traces show some requests still hitting auth token-store with slow fetch.

maya s. (oncall): marking this incident as P1 for follow-through and handoff. I'm going to stay for 15m then hand to jason for deep-dive on auth interactions.

rachel (cust-succ): I've scheduled a call with AcmeHealth for 05:00 UTC to brief and capture impact details.

priya (eng-ml): follow-up action: add more aggressive prefix caching for long streaming sessions and a lightweight backoff on configfetch path to avoid fanout. I'll file an RFC after triage.

sam (eng-platform): next steps I will take:
- bake permanent pool increase and connection pool tuning for configstore-proxy
- add soft rate-limit and queuing at router when control-plane timeouts exceed threshold
- add metrics alert for configfetch fanout
I'll create tickets and link to the incident.

jason (eng-runtime): handing the ongoing investigation (auth traces + long-tail) from maya at 04:36 UTC. maya -> jason handoff: all immediate mitigations applied, customer comms started, monitoring stable but watching.

maya s. (oncall): handing off. please escalate to eng-security if token-store shows suspicious errors. I'm going offline for rest period at 04:45 UTC.

jason (eng-runtime): acknowledged. I'll keep the thread updated. creating incident ticket: INC-2026-4812345678 and assigning to eng-runtime + eng-platform + eng-ml.

deploy-bot: reminder: please include deploy logs for any temporary routing changes as part of the incident ticket.

lee (support): will follow-up with customers after root cause. marking impacted sessions and exporting logs for AcmeHealth.

rachel (cust-succ): adding notes to customer timeline for postmortem.

maya s. (oncall): closing on-call loop, leaving the bridge. last check: streaming_stall_rate 12%, configfetch p99 200ms, auth 429s back to baseline.

jason (eng-runtime): ongoing: deep-dive shows token-store had a short-lived rate-limiter configuration flip that increased 429s under burst. working with security/team owning token-store to roll a fix and add smoother degrade path.

priya (eng-ml): raising follow-up: test harness for end-to-end configfetch failure modes to ensure streaming keeps working during control-plane blips.

anita (product): please schedule a postmortem and include customer impact summary + timeline + mitigation actions.

jason (eng-runtime): noted. will update incident ticket with timeline, trace samples, and mitigation checklist. expected full RCA within 48h.

maya s. (oncall): thanks all — handing off officially to jason.
